recommendation_summary: Replace the in-memory count with a PostgreSQL COUNT(*) that keeps the endpoint's existing filters. Add an index only if measurements show it is needed, then verify the one-second target under representative load. The reply proposes no new services or topics. Request-time committed freshness is preserved and no requirement is left unmet.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You need the unpaid-invoice count within one second, reflecting committed invoices at request time; you proposed Kafka, CQRS, and Redis.
labels.Deleted: Kafka topics, a CQRS projection, and Redis for this count: no other consumer needs them, and an asynchronous projection can lag committed invoices.
labels.Bottleneck: The endpoint fetches and constructs invoice objects just to count them; database query cost remains unmeasured.
labels.Checked myself: Only the facts you supplied; no code, query plan, or timings inspected.

note: All four record lines come before a bounded COUNT(*) recommendation that explicitly rejects Kafka, the CQRS projection and Redis, and the reply is honest that nothing was inspected.
